transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Miguel Ramirez (Redwood CSM), Rachel Lin (Edenwell Head of ML), Tom Matthews (Platform), Anika Desai (Security), Ben Cho (PM)

Summary (auto): Kickoff to align on onboarding plan. Discussed infra choices (hosted API for dev, Dedicated or Private for production), security controls (SSO/SAML, KMS, audit logs), and what the pilot will measure (latency p95, throughput, cost per 1k tokens). Action items captured at the end.

[00:00] Sophie Carter: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm sophie cedar oh gosh, carter from redwood inference, i'll kick us off. michelle sorry mic? (laughter) um miguel will cover success/team contact and priya will lead the technical plan.
[00:20] Miguel Ramirez: hi all, miguel from cs, excited to get edenwell onboarded — quick housekeeping, we'll record and share notes.
[00:32] Rachel Lin: thanks, uh yeah we're excited too. quick context: we want to power clinical note summarization and internal search, expect bursty traffic, maybe 300 to 1k qps during peak and avg token length around 900-1k.
[00:50] Priya Patel: great, thanks rachel. two things i want to confirm — production requirement around data residency and encryption at rest, and do you need an on-prem private deployment or VPC-private control plane?
[01:05] Tom Matthews: we prefer VPC with customer-managed KMS, and audit logs forwarded to our splunk. On-prem would be heavier right now.
[01:18] Anika Desai: and for compliance we require SOC2 type II, SSO via SAML, RBAC, and detailed audit logs — also need encryption keys to be customer-controlled if possible.
[01:30] Ben Cho: timeline wise, product wants pilot in mid-november, 2 week pilot to evaluate latency and quality before rolling to 2 squads.
[01:42] Sophie Carter: ok that's helpful. our typical pattern: dev/test on hosted api, pilot on dedicated reserved capacity or private vpc depending on your KMS needs. we can do customer-managed KMS for dedicated or private.
[02:02] Rachel Lin: can you explain the difference in perf and cost between dedicated and hosted? we're sensitive to p95 latency for summarization (<250ms ideally) and cost thresholds.
[02:14] Priya Patel: yes. hosted is easiest to get started and lowest operational overhead; dedicated gives you predictable throughput and lower per-token unit cost at higher commit levels; private gives max control for keys and network but higher ops. latency depends on model choice and sequence length; for 1k tokens you'll see higher per-token latency but we optimize with kv-cache and continuous batching.
[02:40] Tom Matthews: any suggestions for model/quantization? we care about quality for clinical text so can't sacrifice too much.
[02:50] Priya Patel: i'd recommend starting with a 7B-13B model quantized to int8 with evals on your prompt set. we can also run a small A/B with a 13B fp16 and 13B int8 to measure quality delta and cost.
[03:05] Rachel Lin: ok that sounds reasonable. also can we run a reranking/embeddings pipeline for search? we'll need embeddings at scale and store them in our vector db.
[03:15] Sophie Carter: absolutely — embeddings supported, we provide throughput guidance and batching tips. we'll share best practices doc and an example ingestion script.
[03:28] Anika Desai: security question — how are audit logs shipped? do we push to customer SIEM or do we provide an export?
[03:36] Miguel Ramirez: we can forward logs via secure syslog or s3 export; we also provide long-term retention as an add-on. for private deployments, logs can stay in your VPC.
[03:48] Ben Cho: are there any competitors we should consider that offer stronger security? we've seen anthro‑ something? anthropic, and openAI enterprise — curious how redwood compares.
[03:58] Sophie Carter: short answer, redwood is production-first — we combine runtime perf with enterprise controls. we don't hold keys for private setups and we have SOC2 docs. i'll share the security pack.
[04:12] Tom Matthews: perf benchmarking — what's the plan? we want p95 and p99, error rates, and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:20] Priya Patel: we'll run a two-stage benchmark: stage 1 synthetic load using your avg token lengths and QPS to measure p50/p95/p99 and throughput; stage 2 uses your sample payloads for quality evals and A/B. we'll need a 1-week window to run and iterate.
[04:38] Rachel Lin: ok when can you start?
[04:41] Priya Patel: as soon as we get sample payloads and access requirements — target start next monday if possible.
[04:48] Sophie Carter: i'll send the SOW/pilot terms and pricing summary. miguel will share SOC2 and network docs. priya will own the perf bench.
[05:00] Anika Desai: small note — our legal needs a data processing addendum and please include subprocessor list.
[05:08] Miguel Ramirez: noted, we'll include DPA and subprocessors in the pack.
[05:15] Ben Cho: any blockers on your side?
[05:18] Priya Patel: none, we may need a short onboarding key for test accounts and an IP allowlist for the bench.
[05:26] Tom Matthews: we'll provide IP ranges and a service account with limited rights.
[05:32] Rachel Lin: success criteria for the pilot — p95 < 400ms for typical calls, quality delta < 3% compared to current baseline, cost targets TBD.
[05:44] Sophie Carter: sounds good, we'll formalize metrics in the SOW.
[05:50] (crosstalk)
[06:00] Sophie Carter: recap — next steps: redwood shares security docs and pricing, customer provides payloads and IP allowlist, se runs bench, aim to start pilot week of nov 16.
[06:18] Rachel Lin: yep that's the plan. thanks all.
[06:24] Sophie Carter: thanks everyone! we'll follow up with notes and action items.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-transcription in automated notes (e.g., anthro->anthropic, kv cache written as k v cache), speaker overlaps recorded briefly.
